attributes.board_name: Nebraska State Board of Nursing (Department of Health and Human Services, Licensure Unit)

rules.accepted_credit_types: Nursing CE from an approved provider (accredited by a body such as ANCC or a state board of nursing); related academic courses (1 semester hour = 15, 1 quarter hour = 10 contact hours); CPR/BLS max 4 hours; all hours may be online/home study
rules.alternatives: 20 contact hours in the last 2 years plus 500 practice hours in the last 5 years is the usual route; instead a nurse may have graduated within 2 years, completed a 75-hour board-approved refresher course within 5 years, hold current national specialty certification, or keep a competency portfolio. Graduates of 2-5 years need only the 20 hours.
rules.new_licensee_rule: Nurses first licensed in Nebraska within the past 24 months (current renewal period) need no CE for the first renewal.
rules.audit_note: A percentage of licensees is randomly audited after each renewal period and must then send proof.
rules.notes: RN licenses expire Oct 31 of even-numbered years; the look-back periods start Nov 1, 2 or 5 years before expiration. Waivers exist for qualifying military service and for practicing nurses abroad without CE access. Fee from 172 NAC 2.
rules.rule_quote: Have practiced nursing for at least 500 hours during the past five years AND have completed at least 20 contact hours of nursing continuing education from an approved provider of nursing continuing education within the past two years.
